outputs.description: Reject non-loopback CORS origins and credentialed CORS; host API binding defaults to loopback and rejects non-loopback binding; container mode provider runtime is exposed fail-closed.
Container runtime cannot save credentials or call Ollama; status reports unsupported_runtime. Host mode uses the selected API key or local CLI route.
Provider setup controls are disabled in the container runtime and the host-local setup path is shown.
Agent, non-secret provider config, and job history directories are host-mounted; UI and Jaeger ports bind host loopback; container runtime is identified.
Windows host launcher builds the UI, checks dependencies/port, starts the API hidden on loopback, logs outside the repository, and opens the local app.
v1.2 defines host-local provider support, explicit runtime states, local-only CORS, and persistence behavior.
Windows host setup prerequisites and supported Ollama provider launch flow.

residual_risks: The native Windows launch flow was statically checked but not executed; the selected Python environment must contain requirements.txt, FastAPI, and Uvicorn dependencies.
Docker provider setup remains unsupported by design; Docker UI data paths persist but must not be used to configure Ollama credentials.
LAN deployments remain unsupported until an authenticated API boundary is implemented.

verification.evidence: TypeScript and Vite build passed: 126 modules transformed.
Compose accepted the loopback mappings, runtime marker, and persistent data mounts.
PowerShell parser returned zero syntax errors.

verification.command: Native launcher execution, Docker runtime, secure-store operation, and provider requests
verification.evidence: No app process was launched and no credentials or model requests were used.
